evidence: Judged "If you might be prone to mania or psychosis" over "Any of those reactions, from mania to paranoia, can also point to a vulnerability in you ... any predisposition toward mania or psychosis is a warning sign too ... get help from trusted advisors". "Prone" is a plain word for the paragraph's "vulnerability" and "predisposition", "mania or psychosis" are the paragraph's own words, and "might" lets both a reader who reacted badly and one with a family history see themselves, so no claim is added. It names the situation rather than restating the first sentence and reads as a plain heading in Joel's voice. No linter findings or writer-marked rows, and no tell row PRESENT (the shared "mania or psychosis" is how a skimmer finds the case).
